359	def _validate_manifest(raw: object) -> list[list[Any]]:
360	    if not isinstance(raw, list):
361	        raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest must be a list of "
362	                                "[audit key, event digest] pairs")
363	    manifest: list[list[Any]] = []
364	    last_key: str | None = None
365	    for item in raw:
366	        if not isinstance(item, list) or len(item) != 2 \
367	                or not isinstance(item[0], str) or not item[0] \
368	                or not _is_digest(item[1]):
369	            raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest entries must be "
370	                                    "[non-empty key, 64-digit hex digest]")
371	        if last_key is not None and item[0] <= last_key:
372	            raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest must be ordered by "
373	                                    "key code point without repeats")
374	        manifest.append([item[0], item[1]])
375	        last_key = item[0]
376	    return manifest

378	
379	def _check_extension(old_manifest: list[list[Any]],
380	                     new_manifest: list[list[Any]]) -> None:
381	    # The old snapshot must survive key by key: every anchored key keeps
382	    # its exact digest, while new keys may land anywhere in code-point
383	    # order -- the manifests are compared as key/digest pairs, not by
384	    # position. Fewer entries (retreat), a missing old key (deletion) or
385	    # a changed digest under a known key (rewrite) all surface here.
386	    # Equal manifests (re-query or byte-level log rotation with same
387	    # events) are permitted by the caller and never reach this check.
388	    if len(new_manifest) <= len(old_manifest):
389	        raise BundleMismatchError("a generation only accepts snapshots "
390	                                  "that add new audit events")
391	    new_digests = {audit_key: digest for audit_key, digest in new_manifest}
392	    for audit_key, digest in old_manifest:
393	        if new_digests.get(audit_key) != digest:
394	            raise BundleMismatchError("a generation cannot rewrite, delete "
395	                                      "or reorder an already anchored event")
396

398	def _validate_checkpoint(data: object) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
399	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or list(data.keys()) != list(_ROOT_FIELDS):
400	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint root must be an object with "
401	                                "keys version and generations, in that "
402	                                "order")
403	    version = data["version"]
404	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
405	            or version != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
406	        raise BundleFormatError("unsupported checkpoint version")
407	    generations_raw = data["generations"]
408	    if not isinstance(generations_raw, list):
409	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint generations must be a list")
410	    if not generations_raw:
411	        # export only creates a checkpoint together with its first
412	        # generation, so a persisted empty list is structural damage.
413	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint must carry at least one "
414	                                "generation")
415	
416	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
417	    generations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
418	    # The previous-anchor chain runs across the whole checkpoint: the
419	    # first anchor of a later generation names the last anchor of the
420	    # closed previous generation, so the stream never forks.
421	    previous: str | None = None
422	    for gen_position, generation_raw in enumerate(generations_raw):
423	        is_last_generation = gen_position == len(generations_raw) - 1
424	        if not isinstance(generation_raw, dict) \
425	                or list(generation_raw.keys()) != list(_GENERATION_FIELDS):
426	            raise BundleFormatError("each generation must be an object "
427	                                    "with keys name and anchors, in that "
428	                                    "order")
429	        name = generation_raw["name"]
430	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
431	            raise BundleFormatError("generation name must be a non-empty "
432	                                    "string")
433	        if name in seen_names:
434	            raise BundleFormatError("generation names must not repeat")
435	        if generations and name <= generations[-1]["name"]:
436	            # Names open in strictly ascending code-point order; an
437	            # equal-or-earlier name is a repeat or a regression.
438	            raise BundleFormatError("generation names must not regress")
439	        seen_names.add(name)
440	        anchors_raw = generation_raw["anchors"]
441	        if not isinstance(anchors_raw, list) or not anchors_raw:
442	            raise BundleFormatError("each generation must carry at least "
443	                                    "one anchor")
444	
445	        anchors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
446	        for index, anchor_raw in enumerate(anchors_raw):
447	            is_last_anchor = index == len(anchors_raw) - 1
448	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw, dict) \
449	                    or list(anchor_raw.keys()) != list(_ANCHOR_FIELDS):
450	                raise BundleFormatError(
451	                    "each anchor must be an object with keys manifest, "
452	                    "log_digest, head, previous, closed and digest, in "
453	                    "that order")
454	            manifest = _validate_manifest(anchor_raw["manifest"])
455	            if not _is_digest(anchor_raw["log_digest"]):
456	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor log_digest must be a "
457	                                        "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal "
458	                                        "digest")
459	            head = anchor_raw["head"]
460	            if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
461	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor head must be null or a "
462	                                        "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal "
463	                                        "digest")
464	            declared_previous = anchor_raw["previous"]
465	            if index > 0 and not _is_digest(declared_previous):
466	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor previous digest must be a "
467	                                        "64-digit hexadecimal digest")
468	            if declared_previous != previous:
469	                raise BundleMismatchError("anchor previous digest does not "
470	                                          "continue the chain")
471	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw["closed"], bool):
472	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor closed must be a boolean")
473	            digest = anchor_raw["digest"]
474	            if not _is_digest(digest):
475	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor digest must be a 64-digit "
476	                                        "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
477	            expected = _anchor_digest(manifest, anchor_raw["log_digest"],
478	                                      head, previous, anchor_raw["closed"])
479	            if digest != expected:
480	                raise BundleMismatchError("anchor digest does not match "
481	                                          "its content")
482	
483	            if anchors:
484	                earlier = anchors[-1]
485	                if earlier["closed"]:
486	                    raise BundleMismatchError("a closed anchor cannot be "
487	                                              "followed inside its "
488	                                              "generation")
489	                # Consecutive anchors either pin the same manifest (a
490	                # byte-level log rotation with the events intact, or the
491	                # closing anchor flipping the closed flag) or extend it
492	                # with new keys anywhere in code-point order while every
493	                # anchored pair survives; anything else is a rewrite.
494	                if manifest == earlier["manifest"]:
495	                    if head != earlier["head"]:
496	                        raise BundleMismatchError(
497	                            "a same-snapshot anchor cannot move the root "
498	                            "digest")
499	                    if anchor_raw["log_digest"] == earlier["log_digest"] \
500	                            and anchor_raw["closed"] == earlier["closed"]:
501	                        raise BundleMismatchError("a duplicate anchor "
502	                                                  "changes nothing")
503	                else:
504	                    _check_extension(earlier["manifest"], manifest)
505	            if anchor_raw["closed"] and not is_last_anchor:
506	                raise BundleMismatchError("only the last anchor of a "
507	                                          "generation may be closed")
508	
509	            anchor = {"manifest": manifest,
510	                      "log_digest": anchor_raw["log_digest"], "head": head,
511	                      "previous": declared_previous,
512	                      "closed": anchor_raw["closed"], "digest": digest}
513	            anchors.append(anchor)
514	            previous = digest
515	
516	        if not is_last_generation and not anchors[-1]["closed"]:
517	            # An open generation may only be the last one of the
518	            # checkpoint: any following generation proves it was closed.
519	            raise BundleMismatchError("a new generation can only start "
520	                                      "after the previous one is closed")
521	        generations.append({"name": name, "anchors": anchors})
522	    return generations

555	def _fsync_dir(directory: str) -> None:
556	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
557	    try:
558	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
559	    finally:

562	
563	def _commit_checkpoint(realpath: str, directory: str, payload: bytes,
564	                       old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
565	    # Same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync --
566	    # with a rollback if anything fails after the replace, so a failed
567	    # commit never leaves the new anchor behind. The pre-call bytes are
568	    # staged back over the file (or the file removed when it did not
569	    # exist) and the directory synced again, all while the exclusive
570	    # lock is held; a failed rollback surfaces chained after the first
571	    # error.
572	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
573	        dir=directory, prefix=".audit-proof-", suffix=".tmp")
574	    try:
575	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
576	            handle.write(payload)
577	            handle.flush()
578	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
579	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
580	    except BaseException as first:
581	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
582	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
583	        raise
584	    try:
585	        _fsync_dir(directory)
586	    except BaseException as first:
587	        audit._rollback(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
588	        raise

622	def export(
623	    audit_path: str,
624	    checkpoint_path: str,
625	    generation: str,
626	    final: bool = False,
627	    cursor: str | None = None,
628	    limit: int = audit._DEFAULT_LIMIT,
629	    op: str | None = None,
630	    stage: str | None = None,
631	    key: str | None = None,
632	) -> dict[str, Any]:
633	    """Export a verifiable proof and anchor it in the checkpoint.
634	
635	    ``audit_path`` and ``checkpoint_path`` must be non-empty strings;
636	    ``generation`` must be a non-empty string and ``final`` a boolean.
637	    The search arguments follow :func:`carbon_market.audit.search`. All
638	    argument errors raise ``ValueError`` before any file is read.
639	
640	    A missing audit journal raises ``FileNotFoundError``; so does a
641	    missing parent directory of a checkpoint that must be created. A
642	    version 1 journal, an incomplete digest chain, a malformed
643	    checkpoint, a repeated generation name or an export that reopens a
644	    past generation, an attempt to open a new generation while the
645	    previous one is still open, an export that deletes or rewrites
646	    events of the current generation, or any non-identical export of a
647	    closed generation raises ``ValueError``. Remaining locking or I/O
648	    failures raise ``OSError``.
649	
650	    Returns the offline proof dict: a version 2 envelope whose last
651	    field, ``checkpoint_etag``, is the strong entity tag of the
652	    checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit -- the same
653	    quoted SHA-256 the checkpoint download serves. A repeat of an export
654	    whose content and closed state are identical appends nothing and
655	    returns a proof naming the same anchor and the unchanged snapshot's
656	    tag. With ``final=True`` the appended anchor closes
657	    generation -- it may pin the same snapshot -- after which only the
658	    identical idempotent export (``final=True``) is accepted.
659	    """
660	    for value in (audit_path, checkpoint_path):
661	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
662	            raise ValueError("audit_path and checkpoint_path must be "
663	                             "non-empty strings")
664	    if not isinstance(generation, str) or not generation:
665	        raise ValueError("generation must be a non-empty string")
666	    if not isinstance(final, bool):
667	        raise ValueError("final must be a boolean")
668	    _check_params(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
669	
670	    audit_real = os.path.realpath(audit_path)
671	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
672	    checkpoint_store = _get_store(checkpoint_real)
673	    with checkpoint_store.lock:
674	        # Hold the journal's shared lock and the checkpoint's exclusive
675	        # lock together until the commit lands, so audit.record cannot
676	        # rotate the journal while its bytes are sealed into an anchor.
677	        with audit._file_lock(audit_real, shared=True):
678	            # Read inside the shared flock exactly like the read-only
679	            # audit queries: a racing audit.record is observed as one
680	            # complete document or the other, never a half-replaced
681	            # file. A missing journal surfaces as FileNotFoundError.
682	            with open(audit_real, "rb") as handle:
683	                raw = handle.read()
684	            document = _parse_journal_snapshot(audit_real, raw)
685	            with _file_lock(checkpoint_real):
686	                generations, old_bytes = _read_checkpoint(checkpoint_real)
687	                if generations is None:
688	                    generations = []
689	
690	                params = _params_dict(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
691	                # Compute the page from the exact bytes in hand; this is
692	                # the same filter/pagination audit.search applies.
693	                result = _search_document(document, params)
694	                manifest = _manifest(document)
695	                head = document["head"]
696	                log_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
697	                names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
698	
699	                def identical(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
700	                    return (item["manifest"] == manifest
701	                            and item["log_digest"] == log_digest
702	                            and item["head"] == head)
703	
704	                if generation in names:
705	                    position = names.index(generation)
706	                    if position != len(generations) - 1:
707	                        # A past generation can never be reopened.
708	                        raise ValueError("a past generation cannot be "
709	                                         "exported again")
710	                    current = generations[position]
711	                    anchors = current["anchors"]
712	                    last = anchors[-1]
713	
714	                    if last["closed"]:
715	                        # Once closed the only accepted export is the
716	                        # idempotent one: final stays true and the
717	                        # snapshot is byte-for-byte the same -- events,
718	                        # log bytes and root head. The query may differ,
719	                        # since verify recomputes the page from the
720	                        # embedded log and parameters.
721	                        if not final or not identical(last):
722	                            raise ValueError("a closed generation only "
723	                                             "accepts the identical "
724	                                             "idempotent export")
725	                        return _build_proof(
726	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
727	                            head, True, last["digest"],
728	                            _strong_tag(old_bytes))
729	
730	                    # Still open. Same events, same bytes, same head and
731	                    # not closing: the duplicate export appends nothing
732	                    # and returns the proof of the latest anchor. The
733	                    # manifest must equal the latest anchor's, so an
734	                    # older snapshot cannot mask a retreat.
735	                    if not final and manifest == last["manifest"] \
736	                            and identical(last):
737	                        return _build_proof(
738	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
739	                            head, False, last["digest"],
740	                            _strong_tag(old_bytes))
741	
742	                    # Otherwise append: the manifest grows (strict
743	                    # extension), stays identical with rotated log
744	                    # bytes, or stays identical while final flips the
745	                    # closed flag. A smaller or rewritten manifest is
746	                    # rejected.
747	                    if manifest != last["manifest"]:
748	                        _check_extension(last["manifest"], manifest)
749	                    new_anchor = _make_anchor(manifest, log_digest, head,
750	                                              last["digest"], final)
751	                    anchors.append(new_anchor)
752	                else:
753	                    if generations and not \
754	                            generations[-1]["anchors"][-1]["closed"]:
755	                        raise ValueError("a new generation can only be "
756	                                         "started after the previous one "
757	                                         "is closed")
758	                    if generations and generation <= generations[-1]["name"]:
759	                        raise ValueError("generation names must not "
760	                                         "regress")
761	                    previous_digest = (
762	                        None if not generations
763	                        else generations[-1]["anchors"][-1]["digest"])
764	                    new_anchor = _make_anchor(manifest, log_digest, head,
765	                                              previous_digest, final)
766	                    generations.append(
767	                        {"name": generation, "anchors": [new_anchor]})
768	
769	                payload = _serialize_checkpoint(generations)
770	                _commit_checkpoint(
771	                    checkpoint_real,
772	                    os.path.dirname(checkpoint_real) or ".",
773	                    payload, old_bytes)
774	                # The proof binds the snapshot just committed: while the
775	                # exclusive lock is held the on-disk bytes are exactly
776	                # the committed payload, so its tag is the one a
777	                # download of this checkpoint would serve.
778	                return _build_proof(generation, params, result, raw,
779	                                    log_digest, head, final,
780	                                    new_anchor["digest"],
781	                                    _strong_tag(payload))
782

787	                                "exported fields in their original order")
788	    if not isinstance(data["version"], int) \
789	            or isinstance(data["version"], bool) \
790	            or data["version"] != _PROOF_VERSION:
791	        # A version 1 proof predates the checkpoint snapshot binding and
792	        # is treated as an incomplete proof structure, never as a
793	        # mismatch.
794	        raise BundleFormatError("unsupported proof version")
795	    if not isinstance(data["generation"], str) or not data["generation"]:
796	        raise BundleFormatError("proof generation must be a non-empty "
797	                                "string")
798	    params = data["params"]
799	    if not isinstance(params, dict) \
800	            or list(params.keys()) != list(_PARAM_FIELDS):
801	        raise BundleFormatError("proof params must be the exported query "
802	                                "parameters")
803	    try:
804	        _check_params(params["cursor"], params["limit"], params["op"],
805	                      params["stage"], params["key"])
806	    except ValueError as exc:
807	        raise BundleFormatError(str(exc)) from exc
808	    result = data["result"]
809	    if not isinstance(result, dict) \
810	            or list(result.keys()) != ["events", "next"]:
811	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result must be the exported search "
812	                                "result")
813	    if not isinstance(result["events"], list):
814	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result events must be a list")
815	    next_cursor = result["next"]
816	    if next_cursor is not None and (not isinstance(next_cursor, str)
817	                                    or not next_cursor):
818	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result next must be null or a "
819	                                "non-empty string")
820	    if not isinstance(data["log_bytes"], str):
821	        raise BundleFormatError("proof log_bytes must be a string")
822	    if not _is_digest(data["log_digest"]):
823	        raise BundleFormatError("proof log_digest must be a 64-digit "
824	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
825	    head = data["head"]
826	    if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
827	        raise BundleFormatError("proof head must be null or a 64-digit "
828	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
829	    if not isinstance(data["closed"], bool):
830	        raise BundleFormatError("proof closed must be a boolean")
831	    if not _is_digest(data["anchor_digest"]):
832	        raise BundleFormatError("proof anchor_digest must be a 64-digit "
833	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
834	    checkpoint_etag = data["checkpoint_etag"]
835	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_etag, str) \
836	            or not _ETAG_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_etag):
837	        raise BundleFormatError("proof checkpoint_etag must be a single "
838	                                "strong tag: a quoted 64-digit lowercase "
839	                                "hexadecimal digest")
840	    return data

843	def _search_document(document: dict[str, Any], params: dict[str, Any]) \
844	        -> dict[str, Any]:
845	    # Recompute audit.search's result from an in-memory document so
846	    # verify never needs the journal file itself.
847	    cursor = params["cursor"]
848	    limit = params["limit"]
849	    matches: list[list[Any]] = []
850	    for audit_key, event in document["events"].items():
851	        if cursor is not None and audit_key <= cursor:
852	            continue
853	        if not audit._matches(event, params["op"], params["stage"],
854	                              params["key"]):
855	            continue
856	        matches.append([audit_key, dict(event)])
857	        if len(matches) > limit:
858	            break
859	    if len(matches) > limit:
860	        page = matches[:limit]
861	        return {"events": page, "next": page[-1][0]}
862	    return {"events": matches, "next": None}

865	def _verify_proof(generations: list[dict[str, Any]],
866	                  clean: dict[str, Any],
867	                  checkpoint_real: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
868	    # The cross-checks every verified proof must pass against one
869	    # checkpoint snapshot: the named generation and anchor must be
870	    # recorded, the embedded log bytes must hash to the anchored log
871	    # digest and reparse as a sealed version 2 journal whose manifest
872	    # and root head the anchor pins, and the page must recompute from
873	    # the embedded log and parameters. Every failure here is a
874	    # mismatch, never a format error.
875	    names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
876	    if clean["generation"] not in names:
877	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof generation is not recorded in "
878	                                  "the checkpoint")

923	def verify(checkpoint_path: str, proof: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
924	    """Verify an exported proof solely against the checkpoint.
925	
926	    The journal is not opened: the proof carries the journal's raw
927	    bytes, parameters and result. ``checkpoint_path`` must be a
928	    non-empty string and ``proof`` an object previously returned by
929	    :func:`export`.
930	
931	    The checkpoint bytes are read under the shared lock and their
932	    strong tag is recomputed and confronted with the proof's bound
933	    ``checkpoint_etag`` before anything else: a proof exported against
934	    another snapshot -- older or newer -- mismatches. The embedded log
935	    bytes must hash to the proof's log digest, parse as
936	    a complete version 2 journal whose event manifest and root head
937	    match the anchor the proof names in the named generation of the
938	    checkpoint, and the page must recompute from the embedded log and
939	    parameters. Every anchor chain in the checkpoint is rechecked as
940	    well. Success returns
941	    ``{"events": ..., "next": ..., "generation": ..., "closed": ...}``
942	    -- the original search result together with its generation and
943	    closed state.
944	
945	    A missing checkpoint raises ``FileNotFoundError``; a proof without
946	    the snapshot binding (version 1) or any other structural problem
947	    raises ``BundleFormatError``; any proof or checkpoint mismatch --
948	    including changed log bytes, parameters, page content, cursor, any
949	    digest or a stale snapshot tag -- raises ``BundleMismatchError``;
950	    other I/O failures raise ``OSError``. Both error types are
951	    ``ValueError`` subclasses.
952	    """
953	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_path, str) or not checkpoint_path:
954	        raise ValueError("checkpoint_path must be a non-empty string")
955	
956	    clean = _validate_proof(proof)
957	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
958	    with _file_lock(checkpoint_real, shared=True):
959	        # One locked snapshot: the tag is recomputed from the exact
960	        # bytes that are then parsed and validated, so a racing
961	        # replacement can only yield a self-consistent outcome.
962	        try:
963	            with open(checkpoint_real, "rb") as handle:
964	                raw = handle.read()
965	        except FileNotFoundError:
966	            raise FileNotFoundError(
967	                f"checkpoint file {checkpoint_real!r} does not exist"
968	            ) from None
969	        if clean["checkpoint_etag"] != _strong_tag(raw):
970	            raise BundleMismatchError(
971	                "proof checkpoint_etag does not bind the checkpoint "
972	                "snapshot in hand")
973	        generations = _parse_checkpoint(checkpoint_real, raw)
974	    return _verify_proof(generations, clean, checkpoint_real)

1106	    # checkpoint digest and the candidate node digest; a ready record
1107	    # additionally binds the head digest. Field shape, version, types
1108	    # and the state literal are structural errors; a state string that
1109	    # contradicts its field set or a tag that does not bind its digest

1111	    is_ready = isinstance(data, dict) \
1112	        and list(data.keys()) == list(_TRUST_READY_FIELDS)
1113	    if not is_ready and (not isinstance(data, dict)
1114	                         or list(data.keys())
1115	                         != list(_TRUST_PREPARING_FIELDS)):

1117	                                "preparing or ready fields, in order")
1118	    version = data["version"]
1119	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
1120	            or version != _TRUST_VERSION:
1121	        raise BundleFormatError("unsupported trust state version")
1122	    phase = data["state"]
1123	    if phase not in (_TRUST_STATE_PREPARING, _TRUST_STATE_READY):
1124	        raise BundleFormatError("trust state must be preparing or ready")
1125	    if is_ready != (phase == _TRUST_STATE_READY):
1126	        raise BundleMismatchError("trust state contradicts its fields")
1127	    tag = data["tag"]
1128	    if not isinstance(tag, str) or not _ETAG_RE.fullmatch(tag):
1129	        raise BundleFormatError("trust state tag must be a single strong "
1130	                                "tag: a quoted 64-digit lowercase "
1131	                                "hexadecimal digest")
1132	    checkpoint_digest = data["checkpoint_digest"]
1133	    if not _is_digest(checkpoint_digest):
1134	        raise BundleFormatError("trust state checkpoint digest must be a "
1135	                                "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal digest")
1136	    node_digest = data["node_digest"]
1137	    if not _is_digest(node_digest):
1138	        raise BundleFormatError("trust state node digest must be a "
1139	                                "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal digest")
1140	    if tag != '"' + checkpoint_digest + '"':
1141	        raise BundleMismatchError("trust state tag does not bind its "
1142	                                  "checkpoint digest")
1143	    state = {"state": phase, "tag": tag,
1144	             "checkpoint_digest": checkpoint_digest,

1164	def _inspect_trust_chain(trust_real: str, head_digest: str
1165	                         ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1166	    # Walk the retained sequence from the head node all the way back to
1167	    # the first node and re-check every link from disk, every time:
1168	    #
1169	    # * each node file must exist and reparse; recomputing its digest
1170	    #   over tag, predecessor tag, checkpoint digest and predecessor
1171	    #   node digest must reproduce the name it is referenced by;
1172	    # * each node's predecessor digest is followed to a real node whose
1173	    #   own tag the successor names as its previous_tag;
1174	    # * every node's checkpoint snapshot must exist, its raw bytes must
1175	    #   hit the node's content address, and they must pass the complete
1176	    #   checkpoint structure and anchor-chain validation;
1177	    # * every pair of adjacent snapshots must satisfy the same strict
1178	    #   append-only relation an advancing bundle is checked against --
1179	    #   history continuity is never inferred from node metadata alone.
1180	    #
1181	    # The walk starts from whatever digest the head names, so a head
1182	    # pointing into damaged history can never be masked by the bundle
1183	    # in hand. Returns the entries in chain order, first node to head.
1184	    reversed_entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1185	    seen: set[str] = set()
1186	    digest: str | None = head_digest
1187	    while digest is not None:
1188	        if digest in seen:
1189	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust chain contains a cycle")
1190	        seen.add(digest)
1191	        node_path = os.path.join(trust_real, "nodes", digest + ".json")
1192	        node_raw = _read_trust_file(node_path)
1193	        if node_raw is None:
1194	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust chain references a missing "
1195	                                      "node")
1196	        node = _validate_node(_loads_trust(node_path, node_raw))
1197	        if _node_digest(node["tag"], node["previous_tag"],
1198	                        node["checkpoint_digest"],
1199	                        node["previous_digest"]) != digest:
1200	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust node digest does not match "
1201	                                      "its content")
1202	        snapshot_path = os.path.join(
1203	            trust_real, "snapshots", node["checkpoint_digest"] + ".json")
1204	        snapshot_raw = _read_trust_file(snapshot_path)
1205	        if snapshot_raw is None:
1206	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust chain references a missing "
1207	                                      "checkpoint snapshot")
1208	        if hashlib.sha256(snapshot_raw).hexdigest() \
1209	                != node["checkpoint_digest"]:
1210	            # Same content address, different bytes: evidence is never
1211	            # overwritten or "repaired" from the bundle in hand.
1212	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust checkpoint bytes do not hit "
1213	                                      "their content address")
1214	        generations = _parse_checkpoint(snapshot_path, snapshot_raw)
1215	        reversed_entries.append(
1216	            {"digest": digest, "node": node, "generations": generations})
1217	        digest = node["previous_digest"]
1218	
1219	    entries = list(reversed(reversed_entries))
1220	    anchor_node = entries[0]["node"]
1221	    if anchor_node["previous_tag"] is not None \
1222	            or anchor_node["previous_digest"] is not None:
1223	        raise BundleMismatchError("trust anchor must not name a "
1224	                                  "predecessor")
1225	    for earlier, later in zip(entries, entries[1:]):
1226	        later_node = later["node"]
1227	        if later_node["previous_digest"] != earlier["digest"] \
1228	                or later_node["previous_tag"] != earlier["node"]["tag"]:
1229	            raise BundleMismatchError("trust node predecessor relation "
1230	                                      "does not continue the chain")
1231	        # The on-disk snapshots themselves must form one strict
1232	        # append-only history, not merely look continuous from nodes.
1233	        _check_strict_append(earlier["generations"], later["generations"])
1234	    return entries

1256	def _check_strict_append(old_generations: list[dict[str, Any]],
1257	                         new_generations: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
1258	    # The new checkpoint must be the trusted one plus only appended
1259	    # content: every retained generation survives untouched, the head
1260	    # generation keeps its anchors as a prefix, and at least one anchor
1261	    # or generation is added. The appended content's own legality was
1262	    # already established by the checkpoint validation of the bundle.
1263	    if len(new_generations) < len(old_generations):
1264	        raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint drops trusted generations")
1265	    for position, old_generation in enumerate(old_generations):
1266	        new_generation = new_generations[position]
1267	        if position < len(old_generations) - 1:
1268	            if new_generation != old_generation:
1269	                raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint rewrites a trusted "
1270	                                          "generation")
1271	        else:
1272	            if new_generation["name"] != old_generation["name"]:
1273	                raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint rewrites the "
1274	                                          "trusted head generation")
1275	            old_anchors = old_generation["anchors"]
1276	            if new_generation["anchors"][:len(old_anchors)] != old_anchors:
1277	                raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint rewrites trusted "
1278	                                          "anchors")
1279	    if len(new_generations) == len(old_generations) \
1280	            and len(new_generations[-1]["anchors"]) \
1281	            == len(old_generations[-1]["anchors"]):
1282	        raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint is not a strict append of "
1283	                                  "the trusted head")

1294	def _store_evidence(realpath: str, payload: bytes) -> None:

1298	    # bundle is finishing its interrupted preparation); an existing
1299	    # file holding different bytes is never overwritten or "repaired"

1301	    # evidence stays untouched. A new file commits through the same
1302	    # temporary-file, fsync, atomic replace and directory-fsync
1303	    # discipline as the checkpoint.
1304	    existing = _read_trust_file(realpath)
1305	    if existing is not None:

1309	                                  "holds different bytes")

1359	def _update_trust(trust_dir: str, etag: str, raw: bytes,
1360	                  generations: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
1361	    # Advance the persistent snapshot sequence through its
1362	    # preparing/ready lifecycle, under the trust directory's own
1363	    # in-process lock and exclusive kernel flock so concurrent
1364	    # verifications serialize. Every verification re-inspects the
1365	    # whole retained chain from the first node to the head before it
1366	    # trusts anything, so damaged history or an old bundle replayed
1367	    # against it can never be masked by the bundle in hand.
1368	    trust_real = os.path.realpath(trust_dir)
1369	    store = _get_store(trust_real)
1370	    with store.lock:
1371	        with _file_lock(trust_real):
1372	            # Remember whether the directory existed before this call:
1373	            # a not-yet-existing directory with a usable parent is the
1374	            # first use and anchors through a preparing state committed
1375	            # first; a directory that already exists with neither state
1376	            # nor head is an empty or orphan directory and is never
1377	            # taken over.
1378	            fresh = not os.path.exists(trust_real)
